items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: There's only one man that I do know that used to bite the mouthpiece... and that was George Abad.

ctx.x: You use the double embouchure, you would say, oh. Yeah. Your lip over both upper and lower teeth. Do you know which one of the old musicians did that? For instance, the Teos, do you know how they played Lorenzo Junior? Did he do that or bite on to it?

Well, I don't know, but I do believe this, that the majority of them bite their lip because I was told that that was the right way. There's only one man that I do know that used to bite the mouthpiece, and from playing the horn, from playing the horn a lot, his teeth cut a gutter in the mouthpiece, and that was George Abad.
I don't know. I never, it's hard to tell, you know, unless you're really a clarinetist and look at it, and so I never paid much attention to even Big Eye if he did that. Do you know how he?
